seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Buckeye, AZ: Cotton Fest, the Glow on Monroe light parade, Santa photos, a 33-foot tree show and a church festival.
lede: Buckeye celebrates with Cotton Fest and a tree lighting, a Glow on Monroe electric light parade, Santa photos and a nightly downtown tree show.
celebrates: Downtown Buckeye leads the season. Cotton Fest brings a car show, mariachi music, free Santa photos and the official tree lighting to 6th Street Plaza, with a nod to the history of cotton in the West Valley. A few weeks later, the Glow on Monroe electric light parade rolls down Monroe Avenue. The downtown 33-foot tree puts on a music and light show every half hour, Sundance Park hosts Santa photos with a holiday walkthrough, and The Church at Sun Valley opens its Christmas Festival with hayrides and train rides.
lastyear: Last year, Cotton Fest took place on Saturday, November 29, 2025, in downtown Buckeye. InBuckeye reported free Santa photos from 6 to 8 pm at 6th Street Plaza and the official tree lighting ceremony at 6 pm, produced by Christmas Light Decorators, followed by performances and giveaways. The event was hosted with the Buckeye Main Street Coalition, and the Glow on Monroe electric light parade followed on Saturday, December 13, 2025, at 6:30 pm.
facts: Cotton Fest includes exhibits and storytelling about the rich agricultural heritage of the West Valley, with a History of Cotton segment at the tree lighting. InBuckeye lists the Buckeye Valley Museum among the sponsors. The downtown Christmas tree is 33 feet tall and performs a 15 minute music and light show every half hour. Glow on Monroe follows Monroe Avenue from 2nd Street to Apache Road, a stretch of downtown Buckeye.
trains: Buckeye does not have a holiday train of its own. The Church at Sun Valley's Christmas Festival lists train rides for children, and maricopa Live Steamers in Glendale runs free Holiday Lights Train Rides on select evenings, and our Glendale page lists the dates. For year round train outings, the Arizona Railway Museum in Chandler has historic railroad cars and McCormick-Stillman Railroad Park in Scottsdale has model trains and a miniature railroad.

faq: What is Cotton Fest in Buckeye?

Cotton Fest is Buckeye's downtown holiday kickoff at 6th Street Plaza. It includes a car show, music, kid activities, free Santa photos and the official tree lighting, and it highlights the history of cotton in the West Valley. The Buckeye Main Street Coalition partnered with the town on it last year.
Are there free Christmas events in Buckeye?

Yes. Glow on Monroe is a free event, Santa photos at Cotton Fest are free, and The Church at Sun Valley says its Christmas Festival is free with free hot dogs and popcorn. Food trucks and some extras cost money. Each listing on this page gives the details.
When does the Buckeye tree show run?

The downtown tree runs a music and light show of about 15 minutes every half hour, from sunset until 10 pm, from the Cotton Fest tree lighting until the first of January. There is no fee listed for watching from the public downtown area, and parking is nearby.
Where does the Glow on Monroe parade run?

Along Monroe Avenue in downtown Buckeye, from 2nd Street to Apache Road. Bring chairs or blankets and claim a spot before the parade begins at about 6:30 pm. Downtown shops and restaurants are close by for an early dinner before the lights roll.
Is there a train ride in Buckeye?

The Church at Sun Valley's Christmas Festival lists train rides for children. For larger options, Maricopa Live Steamers in Glendale runs free Holiday Lights Train Rides on select evenings, and the Arizona Railway Museum in Chandler is a year round choice.

intro_html:
Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in Buckeye for 2026, and here is what he found: 6 family events, 2 of them free. The magic runs from November 28 (Cotton Fest and Tree Lighting) through January 1, 2027 (the downtown tree light show), with Glow on Monroe Electric Light Parade (December 12), the Christmas Festival at Festival Foothills Park (December 11) and Santa Photos at Sundance Park (December 5 and 19) along the way. We check every date on the host's own website, and each listing links straight there.
